summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: almost every video gets 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 50 views. The best videos make a robot or a small gadget seem alive with a surprising 'it can't do X, yet it does' idea, and they were posted in the last week. Longer 'how does X work?' questions about public places (lift, mall door, tap, smoke alarm) get far fewer views and almost no saves or shares.
winningPattern: Hindi Instagram Reels about a hands-on maker subject (robot, clap switch, mic, PIR, line follower) with a surprising reversal hook such as 'X can't do Y, only Z' or 'without X the robot falls'. Titles are short, name one object, have a twist and end with an emoji and #shorts. Robot and maker-project videos get the saves and shares; generic everyday-tech 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai?' questions do not.
doMore: Make robot and Arduino-project videos with a 'robot can't do X' twist, since they bring the most views, saves and shares
Use the reversal title format: 'X Nahi, Sirf Y' or 'X Ke Bina Ye Turant Gir Jaata'
Post on Instagram first and treat it as the main platform, then reuse the best ones on YouTube
Show one cause and effect result in the first 2 seconds, such as a robot falling or a light clicking on with a clap
Keep Hindi narration and posting daily, since the Hindi videos all perform better than the English one on Instagram
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai?' videos about mall doors, lifts, taps and smoke alarms
Making several near-duplicate videos on the same sensor (two smoke, two tap, two IR)
Posting the same title and thumbnail style on YouTube and expecting views without changing the hook
